Oral Judgment :
1. Heard learned Advocate for the Appellants, learned Agp for the State/Respondent nos.1 and 2
and learned Advocate for the Acquiring Body - Respondent no.3.

With their assistance, perused the
paper-book.

2. This is an Appeal under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act (for short "the La Act" for) by the
Original Claimants for enhancement in the compensation awarded by the learned Reference Court
by Judgment and Award dated 20.02.2012 awarding the compensation of Rs.1,70,000/- per hectare
for the acquired land of the Appellants to the extent of 3 H 71 R situated at village Malapur, Tahsil
Babhulgaon, District Yavatmal for the purpose of submergence under the Bembla River Project.

The
Notification under Section 4 of the L.A.Act was issued on 14.08.2003.

The Land Acquisition Officer
awarded the compensation at the rate of Rs.79,193/- per hectare.

Being dissatisfied with the said
amount of compensation, the Appellants preferred Land Acquisition Reference No.299/2006.

The
learned Reference Court enhanced compensation with consequential statutory benefits.

3. According to the learned Advocate for the Appellants, the lands from adjoining villages such as
Dighi and Barad were also acquired for the same Project under the same Notification.

He submits
that, the owners of the said lands filed Reference Application and the concerned Reference Court
awarded compensation at the rate of Rs.1,75,000/- per hectare.

Being not satisfied by the said rate,
the Claimants therein, approached this Court in First Appeal Nos.399/2011, 921/2015 and
1062/2014 which came to be decided by Judgments and Orders dated 07.03.2019, 28.04.2016 and
22.03.2016 respectively enhancing the rate of the land to Rs.2,10,000/- per hectare.

He submits
that, the village Malapur is in close vicinity to the said villages and the acquired land of the
Appellants is of similar quality as that of the land which were the subject matter of those appeals,
and therefore, the Appellants are entitled for the same rate.

He submits that, the compensation for
well and trees has been awarded by the learned Reference Court which go to show that, the land of
the Appellants was irrigated land.

He submits that the Appeal deserves to be allowed in terms of the
said Judgments of this Court.
The Appeal is opposed by the learned Advocate for the Acquiring Body.

He submits that, village
Malapur is altogether a different village and the judgments referred by the Advocate for the
Appellants are in respect of different villages and, therefore, the same rate cannot be applied.

He

further submits that, the facilities differ from village to village and Malapur village has a population
of 580.

He submits that, this Court in First Appeal No.405/2012 (Shrirram Devasthan Kopra Jankar
Vs. State of Maharashra and others), which was for the same Project considered all the aspects and
distance between the different villages, in the vicinity of village Panas.

He submits that, in the said
judgment, this Court granted rate of Rs.1,05,000/- per hectare.

He submits that, the Appellants
deserve no enhancement of compensation and the Appeal be dismissed.

5. I have gone through the said judgments relied upon by the learned Advocate for the Appellants
and the learned Advocate for the Acquiring Body.

There is no dispute that the aforesaid judgments
are relating to the Appeals arising out of the Land Acquisition proceedings in which the lands were
acquired for the very same Project and the Section 4 Notification in First Appeal Nos. 921/2015 and
1062/2014 from village Dighi, was 5 fa487.2015 (j).odt of the same date i.e. 14.08.2003.

In the
cross-examination of the Appellants done by the learned Advocate for the Acquiring Body before the
learned Reference Court

, it has clearly come that, village Malapur was at the distance of about 1-1/2
kms from villages Dighi, Nagargaon and Barad.

This clearly indicate that Village Malapur was very
close to the villages Dighi and and Barad.

6. The Judgment dated 22.03.2016 in First Appeal No.1062/2014 indicate that the land which was
the subject matter of acquisition in the said matter was dry crop land.

Perusal of the Judgment of
the learned Reference Court shows that, it considered the rising price trends and observed that, for
determining the land rate of village Malapur on the basis of land for villages Kopra Barad and Kolhi

,
deduction would be proper by keeping in view of the location and fertility of the land and
accordingly, fixed the rate of Rs.1,70,000/- per hectare for the land from Malapur.

As discussed
above, it has come in the evidence that, the distance between village Dighi and village Malapur was
just 1-1/2 kms and when the land of the Appellants and the land of those Appellants were acquired
for the very same Project by the very same Notification, and nothing to show that, there was
difference in the quality of the land in question with 6 fa487.2015 (j).odt the land of the said
Appellants, in my view, the Appellants would be entitled for the said rate of Rs.2,10,000/- per
hectare for the dry land.
7.

The record shows that, there is entry of well and the pipe-line in the 7/12 extract of the Appellants'
land.

There is also no dispute that, the learned Reference Court has awarded the compensation
towards well and trees.
The 7/12 extract also show that, cotton, soyabean and wheat in crop column.

The learned Advocate for the Appellants fairly submits that, the said land was not fully irrigated
land.

It is settled legal position under the law that, the rate for the seasonally irrigated land would be
1.5 more than the rate for the dry crop land.

In this view of the matter, I pass the following order:-
Order
(i) Appeal is partly allowed.
(ii) The Appellants shall be entitled for compensation @ Rs.2,10,000 per hectare for
the dry land and Rs. 3,15,000/- per hectare for seasonally irrigated land i.e. 1.5 ti

(iv) The statutory benefits be calculated on the said amount.
(v) The Appellants would not be entitled for component of interest for the delayed period from 20.2.2012 to 29.04.2015.
